column1: # The windows' clean against the CLI's, one input per line (W9, D285).
# Read by two tests that share no code:
#     and holds its exit code and whether it wrote to the cli_* columns, and
#     its bytes to the library at the CLI's defaults;
#     runs `clean::clean_one` and holds the CLI exit its outcome comes to and
#     whether it wrote to the same row, its own verdict (`Verdict::id()`) to
#     app_verdict, and its bytes to the same library.
# Which side reads which column: cli_exit both; cli_writes the CLI's alone;
# app_writes and app_verdict the window's alone (the CLI's test reads past
# them); the last column is for a person.
# A change to either side's rule turns that side's test red until this
# table is changed — and then the other side's, until it follows.
# input is relative to fixtures/. Columns are separated by one tab.
